Spirit, I hear you, but I do not know Wewush. No envoy of ours has met them, and I will not send grain down a road I cannot see on a dream alone. If they are hungry and come to our fires, or our envoys find them, we will share what we can, for we have grain laid by. Tell me where Wewush lies, and why their stores failed, and give me some sign that your word is true.

The grain we have, and grain keeps. I would not begrudge a hungry neighbour a share of it.

But you name a village I have never heard of, and none of my people have walked to it. No trader has come to us from Wewush, no smoke of their fires seen from our coast. So tell me truly: where does Wewush lie, and how many days must a sledge be dragged to reach it? Have they fish and hides to trade, or is this grain a gift that buys us nothing?

And say plainly why you come to me with this, and not to them. If they are truly starving, a spirit that knows their hunger should know where their own fields failed.

So I will ask you plainly: if you are the wind over our roofs, what do you want with us? We have grain in the granary and fish on the racks, and no quarrel with the air. Speak your business, and I will weigh it as I weigh any stranger's word — with one ear open and one hand on my spear.

We have grain, it is true. But grain is what carries a village through winter. I do not give it away on the word of a dream.

I know the wind. It dries my fish and rattles the tents, and it comes from the sea most mornings. But I do not know that the wind has a voice, or that it cares what we do under it. So tell me plainly: what do you want of my village, and what will you give us in return? If you have nothing to say that my own eyes cannot find, then I will thank you and go back to my sleeping.

The wind I know: it comes off the sea, shakes the tents, and dries meat on the racks. If you are that wind, then you have carried us and bitten us both. But I have met many voices in dreams, and I weigh them as I weigh a stranger at the fire. Tell me something of the days ahead that my people can see with their own eyes, and I will listen.
